conflicts_found: Version numbering: appbrain's 13.430 (S-0001) is CONFIRMED by Apple's first-party version history; fifaworldcupnews's '13.420 released 2026-09-01' is not confirmed by any first-party surface and that source also contradicted itself (13.420 = May 28 'Summer Spotlight'). DLS26-C1 resolved in favour of 13.430 as CURRENT, with 13.420 recorded as an unconfirmed earlier-version claim rather than as a falsehood.
Store update date differs by platform: iOS 'Sep 16' vs Google Play 'Updated on Sep 14, 2026' — a normal staggered rollout, recorded as a platform difference rather than a contradiction.

A Play Store review alleges 'when you sell a player, you don't get your coins back' (S-0012) while FTG's own 12.200 changelog advertises 'Player Recovery - Buy a sold player back within a limited time' (S-0017). These are compatible rather than contradictory (no coin refund on sale, plus a separate time-limited buy-back), but the buy-back's cost and window are unknown, so the pair is recorded as an open question, not resolved by assumption.
iOS Age Rating 13+ and 'Contains: Loot Boxes' vs Android 'Everyone' and 'In-Game Purchases (Includes Random Items)' — the same underlying mechanic disclosed under two platforms' different taxonomies.
entries.confidence_note: Highest-value single fetch of the session so far: it converts the version question from disputed secondary reports into a first-party, dated, checkable record, and it supplies official names for two currencies, a paid season pass, loot boxes, two mechanics (Player Recovery, Special Coach Packs), the client's 15 supported languages, and the developer's own data-collection declarations. Tier remains Speculative under the Mechanism 5 count gate (single origin = FTG, with Apple as the platform displaying it) but origin = DIRECT for every item; promotion path is an independent extraction (client assets in Step 2, or a second unrelated source). The 15-language list is frontier-shaping: it converts 'every language with a DLS26 community' from an open-ended instruction into a bounded, checkable set.
